title: Is selling an AI version of your face to this microdrama startup the future of Hollywood?
lede: Microdrama studio Shortical made a fully AI-generated series starring a digital avatar of actor Aki Avni, its first deal licensing a real person's likeness.

points: In the series Inevitable, Avni plays himself in a plot about an actor who licenses his face to a studio.
Shortical's site invites people to submit social handles to be considered for face-licensing contracts; none have been signed yet.
The company would not disclose Avni's fee, saying it matched a comparable non-AI role, and called royalties case by case.
Rest of World reported Chinese microdrama firms paying between $15 and $700 for a face.
Consultant Jennifer Cooper says AI has cut work in the industry and is pushed more by investors than by viewers.

sections.text: For teams building generative video, consented likeness licensing is turning into a product with contracts and payout infrastructure attached, and the terms creators get are still undefined.
